subject: HIST
title: History – Form 3
source: Harmonised syllabus coverage progression sheet 2026/2027, 2 h/week

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Introduction: political, social and economic life of Cameroon before annexation
Lesson 2: European powers on the coast of Cameroon before annexation

Lesson 4: Activities of European explorers, missionaries, traders, statesmen and soldiers on the rest of the African coast before colonisation
Lesson 5: Motives for the European scramble for Africa: political, social and economic
Lesson 6: Why and how the Germans succeeded in annexing Cameroon
Lesson 7: Attitude of coastal chiefs towards the scramble and annexation of Cameroon
Lesson 8: The Berlin West African Conference: participants, reasons, resolutions and effects on Cameroon
Lesson 9: Consolidation and expansion of German imperial rule in Cameroon
Lesson 10: Reaction of the natives to German annexation: Douala war and land case, Bakweri, Mamfe, Bangwa, Nso
Lesson 11: Political, economic and social development in German Kamerun
Lesson 12: Effects and weaknesses of the Berlin West African Conference on the rest of Africa
Lesson 13: Methods of acquiring African territories: annexation, concession, protectorate, negotiation, military conquest, mandate
Guided work 1: European colonial possessions in Africa
Lesson 14: Reasons for African collaboration with the Europeans
Lesson 15: General causes of African resistance
Lesson 16: Case studies of African resistance: Abyssinia (1896), the Mandinka, the Maji-Maji
Lesson 17: Main features of European colonial policies in Africa, 1900–1945
Lesson 18: British indirect rule: definition and reasons in Northern Nigeria
Lesson 18 (continued): How indirect rule was implemented; merits and demerits; why it succeeded in the north and failed in the south
Lesson 19: French assimilation in Senegal: definition, implementation, benefits and failures (association, differentiation, paternalism)
Lesson 20: Belgian paternalism: definition, reasons, merits and demerits
Lesson 21: Characteristics of white settler colonies in Africa (Kenya, Rhodesia, Algeria)
Lesson 22: Apartheid in South Africa: definition, causes, manifestations
Lesson 23: The fight against apartheid (international and national factors; why apartheid collapsed)
Further study 1: Freedom fighters: Nelson Mandela, Robert Mugabe, Sam Nujoma and others

Lesson 27: Why and how the war was fought in Cameroon; the role of Cameroonians; why Germany was defeated; consequences
Lesson 28: Attempts by Britain and France to set up a condominium; why it failed
Lesson 29: The partition of Cameroon: reasons, how it was done and consequences
Lesson 30: The mandate system, 1922–1939: definition, aims and terms for Britain and France
Lesson 31: Why and how British Cameroons was ruled from Nigeria
Lesson 32: Economic and social development in British Cameroons
Lesson 32 (continued): How and why Britain neglected the development of Southern Cameroons
Lesson 33: French colonial policies in Cameroon (assimilation, association, differentiation, paternalism); administrative set-up

Lesson 35: Resistance against the French mandate: Douala, Bamum, Gbaya (causes, course, consequences)
